production.note: US model years 1970-1971. Old Cars Weekly (Gunnell): "The 426-cube, 425-hp Hemi was a new 'Cuda option" (1970). Supercars.net: "Changes for 1971 were minimal and included a more complex 6 inlet grille design and fender gill louvers." (supercars-hemi-cuda-1970). Old Cars Weekly (2009): "the 1971 Hemi Cudas are even rarer and more expensive" (ocw-hemi-cuda-1970). Reference year 1970.

body.note: "Only 652 1970 Hemi Cuda hardtops were built, and just 14 convertibles were sold in the U.S. market".

aspiration.note: "dual Carter AFB four-barrel carburetors"; no forced induction.

drivetrain.note: Front-engine, rear-wheel drive with a "Dana 9-3/4-inch differential"; inferred.

transmission.note: "New Process A-833 four-speed manual gearbox or the 727 TorqueFlite automatic". The opened pages do not state the TorqueFlite's number of speeds; see reviewNotes.

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (articles, no Chrysler document opened). Manufacturer rating as published in the period: SAE gross (pre-1972 US practice; powerStandard "Other"). Quote (Old Cars Weekly, John Gunnell): "The 426-cube, 425-hp Hemi was a new 'Cuda option". Gold Eagle: "Officially rated at 425 bhp and 490 lb-ft of torque" (goldeagle-hemi-cuda-1970). Supercars.net: "316.9 kw / 425.0 bhp @ 5000 rpm" (supercars-hemi-cuda-1970). Old Cars Weekly (2009): "425 advertised hp" (ocw-hemi-cuda-1970).

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (single numeric source, enthusiast page). Quote (Supercars.net, 1970 Hemi 'Cuda): "Curb Weight | 1642 kg / 3620 lbs". Gold Eagle's "curb weight just under 3,700 lbs" (goldeagle-hemi-cuda-1970) is not a figure and does not count as a second source. Body and transmission not stated (Supercars.net lists the 4-speed manual).

sources.title: Car of the Week: 1970 Plymouth Hemi 'Cuda (John Gunnell)
Car of the Week: 1970 Hemi 'Cuda (1 July 2009)

reviewNotes: Weight rests on one numeric source (Supercars.net). The TorqueFlite automatic is entered as 3-speed, but no opened page states its speed count. No opened page gives a 1971 power or weight figure; Supercars.net says changes for 1971 were minimal.
provisionalNote: Power (425 hp SAE gross) rests on articles (Old Cars Weekly x2, Gold Eagle, Supercars.net), agreeing. Weight (3,620 lb) rests on a single numeric source (Supercars.net). A Plymouth 1970 specification or a major magazine spec panel for the Hemi 'Cuda would replace them.
